detail.longDescription: 137 file types; a single file with nothing to install. Introducing Provost, the free compression and archival tool that can create 119 formats, and open 137 total. It's new custom format packs smaller than ZPAQ, xz, and Zstandard in tests. JPEG, PNG, PDF, DOCX/XLSX, and gzip are unpacked and repacked for ~25% smaller files; ability to encrypt to people's keys or a password; can open archives straight from HTTPS, S3, WebDAV, and SFTP; can search inside archives, including the text of Office files and PDFs; and much more. Q&A --- Is it open source? It is not. Will my .provost files open in five years? I've committed to future releases reading every 0.1.0 archive, and to old compression methods staying readable. Are builds signed? No. The Mac app isn't notarized and the Windows exes are unsigned, so you will see Gatekeeper and SmartScreen warnings. Is the .exe an installer? Nope; it's a stand-alone executable. This is true for all GUI and CLI builds across all three OSes. Is the custom .provost compression fast? Levels 7 to 9 are very slow. There is a built-in benchmark test. How was it built? AI.
